correctness.rationale: For all d>=4,r>=1 over C, in the specified degree-d coefficient cell, the x-degree initial monomial is the squarefree product. On y=0 the singular subscheme is the union over pair strata P^(d-3) of the common zeros of r independent degree-(d-1) G_j. The projective dimension theorem forces dimension >=d-3-r for r<=d-3. At r=d-3, generic complete intersections give (d-1)^(d-3) isolated distinct points on each of binom(d,2) pair strata; triple strata are generically avoided. The mixed y/u Hessian block is invertible with remaining c*s*t block, giving determinant (-1)^(r+1)c^2 and ordinary nodes. For r>=d-2, no projective common zeros occur and Bertini gives smoothness away from the base plane. This covers the universal obstruction, nodal boundary, and existence of smooth generic members.
